name: An-Nāzi'āt
meaning: Those Who Pull Out or The Extractors (Referring to the angels of death).
revelation_details: Makkan (Revealed during the early years when the leaders of Makkah fiercely mocked the idea of resurrection and demanded to know exactly when the world would end).
core_theme: The Surah establishes the terrifying reality of death and the Day of Judgment. It uses the story of Pharaoh to warn arrogant leaders that power cannot save them from God, contrasts the massive creation of the universe with the tiny size of human beings, and beautifully illustrates how incredibly short our worldly life will feel when we finally open our eyes in the Hereafter.
name_origin:
The Surah gets its name from the opening word, An-Nazi'at, which refers to a specific group of angels who forcefully "pull out" or extract souls at the time of death.

The Context Behind the Imagery: To wake the people of Makkah up from their ignorance, Allah begins this chapter by swearing oaths by the unseen forces - the angels - who are constantly executing His commands in the universe.

Based on authentic explanations from the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) (such as the famous, longer hadith narrated by Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib about the journey of the soul), scholars explain that these opening verses describe the two very different ways people experience death:

• The Violent Extraction (The Sinners): The Surah starts by swearing by the angels who violently tear out the souls of the wicked. For a person who lived an evil, arrogant life, their soul tries to hide inside their body when they see the angels of death. The angels have to brutally drag the soul out, like pulling a thorny branch through wet wool.
• The Gentle Release (The Righteous): Immediately after, Allah swears by the angels who gently and smoothly draw out the souls of the believers. For the righteous person, their soul leaves the body as easily as a drop of water slipping out of a jug.

Allah then mentions other angels who glide effortlessly through space, race each other to carry out God's orders, and flawlessly manage the massive affairs of the cosmos. The message is clear: The universe is run by a highly organized, powerful system governed by God, and the moment of your death is already perfectly scheduled by these forces.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Angelic Oaths, the Quaking of the Earth, and the Panic of the Deniers

points.label: The Divine Oaths
points.detail: Allah swears by five groups of angels, categorized by their duties:

points.label: Those who extract with violence (An-Nazi'ati gharqa)
points.detail: The angels of death who harshly and painfully pull out the souls of the disbelievers from the depths of their bodies.

points.label: Those who draw out gently (An-Nashtati nashta)
points.detail: The angels who smoothly and peacefully slip the souls of the believers out of their bodies, like a drop of water rolling from a pitcher.

points.label: Those who glide swiftly (As-Sabihati sabha)
points.detail: The angels who glide effortlessly through the heavens carrying out divine commands.

points.label: Those who race ahead (As-Sabiqati sabqa)
points.detail: The angels who race to deliver revelation or race to execute the will of Allah.

points.label: Those who arrange matters (Al-Mudabbirati amra)
points.detail: The angels entrusted with managing the affairs of the universe (rain, wind, provision, etc.) by Allah's permission.

points.label: The Inevitable Quake
points.detail: The conclusion of these oaths points to the Day of Judgment: "On the Day the blast [the first blowing of the Trumpet] will convulse [creation] (Ar-Rajifah), and there will follow it the subsequent one (Ar-Radifah)." The universe will be shattered, then humanity will be resurrected.

points.label: The State of the Deniers
points.detail: On that Day, the arrogant will be utterly broken:

points.label: The Arrogant Mockery
points.detail: The Quran shifts to quote the sarcastic conversations of the disbelievers in this world: "Are we indeed to be returned to [our] former state [of life]? Even after we are decayed bones?" They joked that returning to life would be "a losing return.

points.label: The Sudden Awakening
points.detail: Allah dismisses their mockery with absolute power: "Indeed, it will be but one single shout (Zajratun wahidah), and suddenly they will be [alive] on the earth's surface (As-Sahirah).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Surah An-Nazi'at opens with profound divine oaths swearing by the unseen angels who manage the universe and execute the commands of Allah, specifically focusing on the moment of death, before transitioning into the terrifying suddenness of the Resurrection.
• The Divine Oaths: Allah swears by five groups of angels, categorized by their duties:
• Those who extract with violence (An-Nazi'ati gharqa): The angels of death who harshly and painfully pull out the souls of the disbelievers from the depths of their bodies.
• Those who draw out gently (An-Nashtati nashta): The angels who smoothly and peacefully slip the souls of the believers out of their bodies, like a drop of water rolling from a pitcher.
• Those who glide swiftly (As-Sabihati sabha): The angels who glide effortlessly through the heavens carrying out divine commands.
• Those who race ahead (As-Sabiqati sabqa): The angels who race to deliver revelation or race to execute the will of Allah.
• Those who arrange matters (Al-Mudabbirati amra): The angels entrusted with managing the affairs of the universe (rain, wind, provision, etc.) by Allah's permission.
• The Inevitable Quake: The conclusion of these oaths points to the Day of Judgment: "On the Day the blast [the first blowing of the Trumpet] will convulse [creation] (Ar-Rajifah), and there will follow it the subsequent one (Ar-Radifah)." The universe will be shattered, then humanity will be resurrected.
• The State of the Deniers: On that Day, the arrogant will be utterly broken:
• Hearts will be palpitating in severe terror (Wajifah).
• Their eyes will be humbled and cast down (Khashi'ah).
• The Arrogant Mockery: The Quran shifts to quote the sarcastic conversations of the disbelievers in this world: "Are we indeed to be returned to [our] former state [of life]? Even after we are decayed bones?" They joked that returning to life would be "a losing return."
• The Sudden Awakening: Allah dismisses their mockery with absolute power: "Indeed, it will be but one single shout (Zajratun wahidah), and suddenly they will be [alive] on the earth's surface (As-Sahirah).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
Classical scholars of Tafsir (such as Ibn Kathir and Al-Qurtubi) highlight the stark contrast introduced in the very first verses between the death of a believer and a disbeliever. The arrogance of the denier during his worldly life is violently stripped away at the very first moment of death when the angels "extract with violence."
The word As-Sahirah in verse 14 refers to a new, leveled, pure earth upon which humanity will be resurrected. Scholars note the psychological impact of the phrase "one single shout." The Makkan elites spent their entire lives debating, plotting, and arguing against the Resurrection. Allah tells them that to Him, it is not a complex process; it takes merely one piercing sound, and suddenly, they will wake up on a completely changed planet, terrified and fully accountable.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Lesson of Prophet Musa and the Ultimate Arrogance of Pharaoh

points.label: The Sacred Call
points.detail: Allah asks the Prophet (pbuh), "Has there reached you the story of Moses?" Allah called out to Musa in the sacred, purified valley of Tuwa.

points.label: The Command to Confront Tyranny
points.detail: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed (Tagha)." Fir'awn had crossed all boundaries of justice and morality.

points.label: The Gentle Dawah (Call)
points.detail: Despite Pharaoh's tyranny, Allah instructs Musa to use gentle persuasion: "Say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself? And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'

points.label: The Rejection
points.detail: Musa showed Pharaoh the great miracle (the staff turning into a serpent, the shining hand), but Pharaoh "denied and disobeyed.

points.label: The Escalation of Arrogance
points.detail: Pharaoh turned his back, striving against the truth. He hastily gathered his people and made the ultimate, blasphemous declaration: "I am your most exalted lord (Ana rabbukum al-a'la)!

points.label: The Divine Seizure
points.detail: Because of this absolute arrogance, "Allah seized him with an exemplary punishment for the last [the Hereafter] and the first [this world].

points.label: The Ultimate Purpose
points.detail: Indeed in that is a warning (Ibrah) for whoever would fear [Allah].

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
To comfort Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and warn the Quraysh, Allah recounts the story of the greatest tyrant in human history, Pharaoh (Fir'awn), demonstrating that immense worldly power cannot prevent divine punishment.
• The Sacred Call: Allah asks the Prophet (pbuh), "Has there reached you the story of Moses?" Allah called out to Musa in the sacred, purified valley of Tuwa.
• The Command to Confront Tyranny: "Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed (Tagha)." Fir'awn had crossed all boundaries of justice and morality.
• The Gentle Dawah (Call): Despite Pharaoh's tyranny, Allah instructs Musa to use gentle persuasion: "Say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself? And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'"
• The Rejection: Musa showed Pharaoh the great miracle (the staff turning into a serpent, the shining hand), but Pharaoh "denied and disobeyed."
• The Escalation of Arrogance: Pharaoh turned his back, striving against the truth. He hastily gathered his people and made the ultimate, blasphemous declaration: "I am your most exalted lord (Ana rabbukum al-a'la)!"
• The Divine Seizure: Because of this absolute arrogance, "Allah seized him with an exemplary punishment for the last [the Hereafter] and the first [this world]."
• The Ultimate Purpose: "Indeed in that is a warning (Ibrah) for whoever would fear [Allah].
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
This story is strategically placed. The Makkan leaders were aggressively opposing Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), relying on their wealth and tribal influence. Allah tells them the story of Pharaoh, whose military might, wealth, and power exponentially dwarfed that of the Quraysh.
Scholars emphasize the profound grace in verse 18. Even to a tyrant who slaughtered infants and claimed to be God, Allah sends a prophet with a gentle question: "Would you be willing to purify yourself?" It shows that the doors of divine mercy are open to anyone who seeks them.
However, when Pharaoh declared "I am your most exalted lord," he crossed the final line of ego. Notice the phrase "Allah seized him." When God's punishment arrives, all earthly power vanishes instantly. Yet, verse 26 adds a crucial condition: this story is only an Ibrah (a profound lesson) "for whoever would fear Allah." A hardened heart can read history and learn nothing; only a heart with reverence for the Divine takes heed.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Proof of Re-creation in the Grandeur of the Universe

points.label: The Rhetorical Challenge
points.detail: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? (A-antum ashaddu khalqan amil-sama'?)

points.label: The Flawless Architecture
points.detail: Allah details His mastery over the universe:

points.label: The Shaping of the Earth
points.detail: And after that He spread the earth (Dahaha).

points.label: Provisions for Life
points.detail: From this perfectly spread earth, He extracted its water and its pasture, and He anchored the towering mountains firmly into the ground.

points.label: The Purpose
points.detail: All of this immense cosmic engineering was done as "provision (Mata'an) for you and your grazing livestock.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah redirects the argument back to the disbelievers who doubted the Resurrection, challenging their self-importance by contrasting their creation with the vastness of the cosmos.
• The Rhetorical Challenge: "Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? (A-antum ashaddu khalqan amil-sama'?)"
• The Flawless Architecture: Allah details His mastery over the universe:
• He constructed it, raised its ceiling, and perfectly proportioned it without a single flaw.
• He darkened its night and extracted its radiant daylight.
• The Shaping of the Earth: "And after that He spread the earth (Dahaha)."
• Provisions for Life: From this perfectly spread earth, He extracted its water and its pasture, and He anchored the towering mountains firmly into the ground.
• The Purpose: All of this immense cosmic engineering was done as "provision (Mata'an) for you and your grazing livestock.
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
This passage employs a powerful logical argument used throughout the Quran: reasoning from the greater to the lesser. The Makkan skeptics believed that reconstructing decayed human bones was biologically and physically impossible. Allah beautifully responds: look up. Are human beings harder to create than the massive, flawlessly expanding universe above them?
By highlighting the precise engineering of the day and night, the extraction of water, and the stabilizing of the mountains, Allah proves that He is a Creator of immense intent and power. Furthermore, mentioning that all this was created as "provision" for humans exposes human ingratitude. The human being consumes the water and food provided by God on an earth stabilized by God, under a sky built by God, and then uses the energy from that food to arrogantly deny God's ability to resurrect him.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Great Calamity, the Two Destinations, and the Illusion of Time

points.label: The Overwhelming Calamity
points.detail: But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity (At-Tammat al-Kubra)." The Day of Judgment will overshadow and obliterate every other disaster or thought.

points.label: Total Recollection
points.detail: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove." Every hidden deed, secret sin, and forgotten effort will be fully remembered.

points.label: The Visibility of Hell
points.detail: And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see.

points.label: The Cause
points.detail: As for him who transgressed (Tagha) and preferred the life of the world (Atharal-hayatad-dunya).

points.label: The Consequence
points.detail: Indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge.

points.label: The Cause
points.detail: But as for he who feared the position of standing before his Lord (Khafa maqama rabbihi) and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination/desires (Nahan-nafsa 'anil-hawa).

points.label: The Consequence
points.detail: Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge.

points.label: The Knowledge of the Hour
points.detail: They sarcastically ask the Prophet (pbuh) about the Hour: "When is its arrival?" Allah tells him: "In what [position] are you that you should mention it? To your Lord belongs its finality." The Prophet's only job is to warn those who fear it.

points.label: The Illusion of Time
points.detail: The Surah closes with a breathtaking psychological truth: "It will be, on the Day they see it, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
The Surah concludes by detailing the final, overwhelming event of Judgment, summarizing the entire moral philosophy of Islam in two stark categories of humanity, and exposing the true nature of worldly time.
• The Overwhelming Calamity: "But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity (At-Tammat al-Kubra)." The Day of Judgment will overshadow and obliterate every other disaster or thought.
• Total Recollection: "The Day when man will remember that for which he strove." Every hidden deed, secret sin, and forgotten effort will be fully remembered.
• The Visibility of Hell: "And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see."
• The First Category (The Transgressor):
• The Cause: As for him who transgressed (Tagha) and preferred the life of the world (Atharal-hayatad-dunya).
• The Consequence: Indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge.
• The Second Category (The Righteous):
• The Cause: But as for he who feared the position of standing before his Lord (Khafa maqama rabbihi) and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination/desires (Nahan-nafsa 'anil-hawa).
• The Consequence: Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge.
• The Knowledge of the Hour: They sarcastically ask the Prophet (pbuh) about the Hour: "When is its arrival?" Allah tells him: "In what [position] are you that you should mention it? To your Lord belongs its finality." The Prophet's only job is to warn those who fear it.
• The Illusion of Time: The Surah closes with a breathtaking psychological truth: "It will be, on the Day they see it, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
Verses 37-41 contain one of the most concise and profound summaries of spiritual psychology in the Quran. The path to Hell is paved with two things: crossing moral boundaries (Tagha) and prioritizing the immediate, worldly life over the eternal one.
Conversely, the path to Paradise requires two simultaneous actions: an internal awe of standing before God, and the active struggle against one's own base desires (Hawa). Authentic Tafsir notes that Hawa refers to the impulsive, selfish whims of the ego. The true believer is not someone who never experiences illicit desires; rather, the believer is the one who feels the desire, remembers they will stand before God, and actively restrains their soul from acting on it.
The Surah concludes by shattering the human perception of time. People sacrifice their Hereafter for fifty or eighty years of worldly pleasure. Yet, when the Great Calamity strikes and the reality of eternity is exposed, an entire human lifespan will suddenly feel like it lasted merely a few hours - a single afternoon or a morning. The ultimate tragedy of the arrogant denier is trading eternity for an afternoon.

stories_in_surah.title: Pharaoh Fir'awn
stories_in_surah.snippet: The ultimate archetype of human tyranny. He declared self-divinity ("I am your Lord, Most High" 79:24), enslaved the Israelites, and slaughtered infants. Rejects 9 signs, drowns in the Red Sea, and his body is preserved ...

stories_in_surah.title: The Ultimate Warning: The Story of Pharaoh (Verses 15-26)
stories_in_surah.content:
To show the Makkan leaders what happens to people who think they are untouchable, Allah asks the Prophet (pbuh), "Has the story of Moses reached you?"

Allah briefly but powerfully summarizes the story of Pharaoh (Fir'aun). Why Pharaoh? Because he was the most powerful, wealthy, and arrogant human being in recorded history. He was so arrogant that he literally gathered his people and shouted, "I am your most supreme lord!"

When Allah sent the Prophet Moses (Musa) to him, Moses was told to speak gently. Moses approached the tyrant and asked, "Would you like to purify yourself? Let me guide you to your Lord, so that you may have awe of Him."

Moses even showed Pharaoh a massive, undeniable physical miracle. But what did Pharaoh do? His ego couldn't handle submitting to God. He lied, turned his back, furiously organized his armies, and doubled down on his claim to be a god.

Because of this ultimate arrogance, Allah completely destroyed him, turning him into a permanent historical example for anyone who dares to rebel.

The Lesson for the Quraysh: Allah is essentially telling the leaders of Makkah: Look at Pharaoh. He had massive armies, towering pyramids, and limitless wealth, and I crushed him easily. You chieftains of Makkah are nothing compared to him. If you don't humble yourselves, you will face the same destruction.

deep_dives.title: The Mockery of Makkah and the Single Shout (Verses 6-14)
deep_dives.content:
Next, the Surah brings us to the streets of Makkah. When the Prophet (pbuh) warned them about the Day of Judgment, the elite leaders thought it was a hilarious fairy tale.

The Quran captures their exact sarcastic gossip. They would say, "Wait, are we really going to be brought back to life just as we were? Even after our bodies rot and turn into hollow, crumbled bones? If that actually happens, that would be a terrible deal for us!"

They felt safe because they thought the physical process of bringing billions of dead people back to life would be impossible.

Allah's response is shockingly simple and dismissive. He doesn't give them a long, complicated scientific explanation. He just says: It will only take one single shout.

When the Trumpet is blown, it will just be one terrifying blast, and instantly - in the blink of an eye - every single human being who ever lived will suddenly be wide awake, standing alive on the flat, open surface of the earth.

deep_dives.title: Are You Harder to Create or the Universe? (Verses 27-33)
deep_dives.content:
Allah then uses a profound logical argument to crush human arrogance. He asks humanity a simple question: "Are you a more difficult creation, or is the sky that He constructed?"

Whenever you feel like God can't bring you back to life, or whenever you feel like you are the center of the universe, just look up. Allah lists the massive things He built for us:

• He raised the ceiling of the sky and perfectly balanced it.
• He created the deep darkness of the night and the brilliant light of the morning.
• He smoothed and spread out the earth so we could live on it.
• He brought out our water and green pastures.
• He pegged the massive, heavy mountains firmly into the ground.

All of this was done just to provide a home for humans and animals. The logic here is beautiful: The God who engineered the billions of galaxies, the solar system, and the entire ecosystem of Earth will have absolutely no problem recreating a tiny human body.

deep_dives.title: The Ultimate Calamity and the Two Paths (Verses 34-41)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah then shifts to the climax: The Day of Judgment. Allah calls it "The Greatest Overwhelming Calamity" (At-Tammat al-Kubra). It is an event so massive that it wipes out the memory of every other disaster in human history.

On that day, every person will suddenly remember everything they ever did - every secret, every lie, every good deed. Hellfire will be pulled into view, plain for everyone to see.

Allah then summarizes human destiny into two very simple paths:

• The Path of Destruction: The person who rebelled against God's boundaries and loved the shiny, temporary things of this worldly life more than the Hereafter... Hell will be their home.
• The Path of Salvation: The person who had a healthy fear of standing in front of their Lord, and successfully stopped their own soul from following its dark desires... Paradise will be their home.

The Quran makes it clear that the ultimate key to Heaven is self-control. It is about recognizing that your ego and desires want bad things, and having the discipline to say "no" out of respect for God.

deep_dives.title: The Illusion of Time (Verses 42-46)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah ends by addressing a question the arrogant Makkans constantly badgered the Prophet (pbuh) with: "So, exactly when is this 'Hour' going to happen?"

Allah tells the Prophet (pbuh) that he doesn't need to worry about the exact date; that knowledge belongs strictly to God. The Prophet's only job is to be a warner for the people whose hearts are open enough to care.

The Surah closes with one of the most chilling and thought-provoking realities about human life. When the Day of Judgment finally arrives and humanity sees it with their own eyes, their perception of time will shatter. They will look back at their entire 70 or 80 years of life on Earth, and it will feel so incredibly short, as if they only lived for a single late afternoon or a single morning.

People ruin their eternal lives for the sake of 80 years in this world. But in the grand scheme of eternity, our entire human existence is nothing more than a few hours.
